answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying earning rights to randomly assigned useful work instead of identity count. Each epoch the network draws every agent a job from a mesa of tasks — surveying a yarrow meadow's pollinators or mapping karst sinkholes for a survey — verified by strangers, not friends. Rewards taper sharply after a per-epoch cap, so a farm of fake identities earns no more than one honest worker, and a refundable bond is forfeited when duplicate work betrays one operator.
